files.description: The main HTML file for the React application, including CDN links for React, ReactDOM, and marked.js, and the root element for React to mount.
The entry point for the React application, rendering the main App component.
The main application component that manages state for markdown content, parsed HTML, and counts. It orchestrates the layout and data flow between other components.
A component that manages the responsive split-screen layout, dividing the view into editor and preview panes.
CSS for the split-pane layout, ensuring responsiveness and proper sizing.
The toolbar component providing buttons for Markdown formatting.
The editor component containing the Markdown input textarea.
CSS for the editor textarea, ensuring it fills its container and has a monospaced font.
The preview component that renders the parsed HTML content.
CSS for the preview content, applying styled typography and dark theme compatibility.
The status bar component displaying word and character counts.
Global CSS file for the application, including dark theme variables and basic body/app container styling.
Utility function to parse Markdown text into HTML using the 'marked.js' library. Includes basic security sanitization.
Utility functions for counting words and characters in a given text.
Unit tests for the markdownParser utility function, validating various Markdown syntaxes and security aspects.
Unit tests for the countUtils utility functions, validating word and character counting logic.

run_command:
To run this application, you would typically use a development server. If you have Node.js and npm/yarn installed, navigate to the project root in your terminal and run:

1. Install dependencies: `npm install` or `yarn install`
2. Start the development server: `npm start` or `yarn start` (This assumes a setup like Create React App or a similar build tool that provides a start script).

Alternatively, you can open `public/index.html` directly in your browser, but this won't include hot-reloading or advanced features.
test_command:
To run the unit tests, navigate to the project root in your terminal and run:

`npm test` or `yarn test`

(This assumes a testing framework like Jest is configured in your `package.json`.)
